gaps: No separate Spec review result was supplied; the Solution Gate contract was used as the implementation oracle.

lenses.reason: No matcher, parser, lookup, or semantic data source was replaced.

lenses.reason: Covered default and isolated contexts, two isolated sessions, foreign targets, daemon restart, Chrome restart, state save and restore, recording child contexts, explicit close, and late isolation enablement.

lenses.name: Resolution-rule consistency across consumers
lenses.reason: No value-resolution rule from ambiguous user input changed; BrowserContext ownership was reviewed through the boundary and flag-propagation lenses.

lenses.name: Shell re-parse append domain
lenses.reason: No shell command parsing or flag injection into shell text changed.

lenses.name: Emission channel and one-shot latch reachability
lenses.reason: No warning channel or one-shot latch was added.

lenses.name: Shim hermeticity
lenses.reason: No external binary shim was added.

lenses.name: Deliberate-default check
lenses.reason: Verified isolation remains opt-in and ordinary shared-Chrome behavior remains unchanged without the flag.

lenses.name: Fresh-seam scan
lenses.reason: No runtime or framework patch introduced a new application signal.

lenses.name: Substrate differential corpus
lenses.reason: The ownership guard had not failed two prior review rounds on the same class.

lenses.name: Reference-implementation oracle
lenses.reason: The implementation delegates isolation to Chrome BrowserContexts instead of reimplementing an external semantic contract.

lenses.name: New-failure-outcome propagation
lenses.reason: A late isolateContext request on an existing non-isolated connection now returns a reconnect-required error; the caller path was verified to leave sticky state unchanged.

lenses.name: Flag-propagation dispatch sweep
lenses.reason: Traced --isolate-context and AGENT_BROWSER_ISOLATE_CONTEXT through parsing, config, launch envelopes, daemon options, connect, MCP, schema, help, docs, and skill surfaces.

lenses.name: Error-path forcing
lenses.reason: Forced late isolation enablement, missing context after Chrome restart, unpersisted-context rollback, foreign auto-attach, internal shutdown, and explicit close.

lenses.name: Non-destructive recovery
lenses.reason: Verified a missing persisted Chrome context creates a clean owned replacement, reapplies configured state, and never falls back to or damages the default context.

lenses.name: Cancellation and timeout hygiene
lenses.reason: The change adds no new timeout, polling ceiling, or cancellable request contract.

lenses.name: Boundary pipeline trace
lenses.reason: Traced context ownership through CLI and MCP input, daemon state, CDP discovery and events, target producers, state operations, persistence, recording, shutdown, and close.

lenses.name: Substrate verification
lenses.reason: Observed distinct cookies, localStorage, sessionStorage, targets, context IDs, restart survival, context recreation, child cleanup, and owned-context disposal in real Chrome.

lenses.name: Dogfood the built artifact
lenses.reason: Drove three real-Chrome E2Es covering parallel isolated sessions, restart and close, Chrome restart and restore, plus recording-child shutdown cleanup.

lenses.name: Docs-behavior parity
lenses.reason: Checked README, CLI help, commands docs, configuration, CDP mode, sessions docs, schema, MCP, and skill prose against the implemented scope and lifecycle.

lenses.name: Demonstrative example
lenses.reason: The two-session shared-Chrome examples require isolated contexts to preserve distinct login state and match the driven Chrome workflow.

lenses.name: Choice audit
lenses.reason: Audited every .decisions.tsv row, including fail-closed binding versioning, explicit-close ownership, rollback transfer, and shutdown cleanup ordering.

lenses.name: Complexity budget
lenses.reason: Owned-context membership uses bounded context sets and linear filtering over browser targets; no nested per-target scan or unbounded structure was introduced.

deterministic.reason: This report fingerprints committed HEAD ee68b3c.
The commands documentation surface initially omitted --isolate-context and was updated.
All three isolation E2Es passed together.
Moving the sticky isolate_context mutation before validation made the E2E fail; restoring validation-before-mutation passed.
Removing child-context disposal made the shutdown E2E fail; restoring cleanup passed.
Seven earlier independent mutations failed as intended.
127 changed symbols, top 200 impacted items, and 8019 edges; 2402 unresolved calls, 74 unmapped SCIP entries, and rust-analyzer duplicate-symbol errors mean the map under-covers.

findings.claim: The canonical commands page omitted the new --isolate-context flag.
findings.evidence: The surface sweep found no entry in docs/src/app/commands/page.mdx. The page now lists the flag and the docs build passes.

findings.claim: Signal and idle shutdown could orphan a recording child BrowserContext and autosave from the child instead of the persisted primary context.
findings.evidence: Those daemon exits bypassed the internal shutdown command. prepare_internal_daemon_shutdown now stops recording, disposes registered child contexts, preserves the primary context, and runs before autosave on every internal exit. Removing disposal makes the real-Chrome shutdown E2E fail.
findings.layer: daemon lifecycle ordering and BrowserContext ownership
findings.path: daemon shutdown branch -> prepare_internal_daemon_shutdown -> dispose_child_contexts -> auto_save_restore_state -> close_all_browser_backends

findings.claim: A late isolateContext request on an already-open non-isolated connection could set sticky isolation state without reconnecting.
findings.evidence: The command path mutated state.isolate_context before proving the current BrowserManager was isolated. It now returns a reconnect-required error first and leaves state false; moving the mutation before validation makes the E2E fail.
findings.layer: daemon command validation and sticky state mutation
findings.path: command isolateContext -> existing BrowserManager isolation check -> state.isolate_context mutation

exemptions.evidence: This repository's release PR owns changelog entries; the feature surfaces are documented in README, CLI help, web docs, schema, MCP, and skill data.
